title: Spring dates gave no clear later-year autumn colour prediction gain in four Swiss beech samples
abstract: We tested whether spring leaf unfolding improved later-year autumn colour predictions beyond station, linear time and seasonal temperature. We used 3,428 paired station-years at 72 Swiss beech stations in 1961-1990 and 1991-2020. Separate western and eastern models trained on earlier years and tested ten later years in each period. The four tests used 1,232 evaluation pairs. Adding spring dates changed mean absolute error by -0.024 to +0.172 days. All four nominal 98.75 percent two-year block bootstrap intervals included zero. Four checks gave no clear repeated gain. This is a new prediction test on records used in prior campaign studies. It does not show that spring has no biological effect. Short test periods, long-record station selection, coarse temperature and unknown observer changes limit inference. Realised summer and September weather make these conditional hindcasts, not spring forecasts. Air pollution and weather extremes were not tested. Code, source hashes, aggregate losses, validation and a figure are included. External source databases remain outside the package.

display.caption: Adding spring dates gave no clear repeated error reduction in four later-year tests. Negative values mean lower mean absolute error. Bars show approximate two-year block bootstrap intervals at a nominal 98.75 percent level.
